composers_checked.name: Stamitz, Carl
composers_checked.note: Floor from Apple Music track lists and MusicBrainz. Gap check against the recorded repertoire (Op. 4/14, Op. 8, Op. 19, trios): added Op. 8 No. 3, Op. 19 Nos. 2–3, a second trio for two flutes and cello and two quartets for two flutes, viola and cello. No public complete work list found.

composers_checked.name: Rolla, Alessandro
composers_checked.note: Floor from Apple Music track lists (Pan Classics box 2020, Hungaroton, Dynamic, Tactus, Brilliant); MusicBrainz holds few Rolla recordings. No public work list (the Bianchi-Inzaghi catalogue is not online); gap check against the recordings found: added the six Tactus flute quartets and the Piccolo quartetto BI 425.

composers_checked.name: Gluck, Christoph Willibald
composers_checked.note: Gap check against the Wikipedia list of compositions and the Gluck-Gesamtausgabe work register (seven trio sonatas: the six of 1746 and one in F): nothing missing. MusicBrainz and Apple Music: two complete recordings.

note: Stamitz: 1) Opus numbers follow IMSLP (DTB Op. 4 = Sieber Op. 14); recordings use both, given in aka. 2) Op. 4 Nos. 2 and 5 ('concertant' quartets) are kept on the strength of one recording by a chamber orchestra (NZSO CO, Naxos); string-orchestra question: Nos. 1 and 4 'à grand orchestre' skipped, recorded only by chamber orchestras. 3) The census counted 5 works on the Op. 14 trios page because it took 'Trio in G major for 2 Flutes and Cello' (Hortus Musicus 'Op. 14 No. 1') for its first trio; IMSLP says it is a different Op. 14, and the movements differ, so all six Welcker trios are kept and the flute trio separately. 4) Op. 8 scoring: the census read IMSLP's alternatives as 'clarinet, bassoon, horn, violin'; the print is clarinet (flute, oboe, violin), violin, viola (horn), cello (bassoon). 5) The two quartets for two flutes, viola and cello 'Op. 19' and the second G-major flute trio come only from track lists (medium confidence). 6) Not added for lack of identification: 'Horn Trio in E-flat major' and 'Flute Quartet No. 1 in C major' (cpo, Proprius), scoring and catalogue number unknown. Rolla: 1) The two IMSLP pages of the first book of trios (BI 348/342/343 and BI 351/344/349) are scans of the same Imbault print (plate 447); kept once as Op. 1 Nos. 1–3, the other page skipped as duplicate. The Pan Classics and Hungaroton recordings of Nos. 1–3 give different slow-movement titles, so one of them may be another set in the same keys: worth a score check. 2) The IMSLP page 'Op. 2 (BI 346, 341, 347)' is the second book of Op. 1 (IMSLP comment); kept as Op. 1 Nos. 4–6 to match the Hungaroton 'Op. 1 complete'. 3) BI 397, 405, 410 label both the Op. 2 quartets and the Ricordi 1828 trios (on IMSLP and on the Pan Classics box); the trios are titled without BI numbers. 4) Op. 2 No. 2 is F minor on IMSLP and 'F major' on Apple Music; IMSLP followed. 5) Op. 5: IMSLP numbers G, D minor, E-flat as Nos. 1–3, Dynamic as Nos. 5, 4, 3; IMSLP gives the G major three movements, the recording four. 6) Six Tactus flute quartets added without catalogue numbers (not found; one web search). 7) Not added for lack of identification or scoring: Divertimento ossia Sestetto BI 433 and Divertimento BI 427a (Dynamic 2008), Concertino a tre (MusicBrainz), and the trios for two clarinets and viola and the basset-horn concerto with string quartet on 'Alessandro & Antonio Rolla' (Brilliant 2026), where the composer of each piece is not given. Gluck: Wikipedia marks Wq. 53 and the E major Wq. 54 sonata 'mis-attributed', citing the Gluck-Gesamtausgabe register; that register (checked) lists the six 1746 sonatas and an F major sonata (with 'Korrigenda'), but no E major sonata. Kept all eight as recorded under Gluck's name; the E major's note flags the doubt. Owner may want an expert check of the Wq. 53 attribution.
